content: Insulated packaging systems that meet the specifications of Packing Instruction 202 and contain refrigerated liquid nitrogen fully absorbed in a porous material are exempt from these regulations. This exemption is valid provided that the design of the insulated packaging prevents the accumulation of pressure within the container and does not allow the release of any refrigerated liquid nitrogen, regardless of the orientation of the packaging. Additionally, any outer packaging or overpack used must be sealed in a manner that prevents pressure buildup within the packaging or overpack. When such packaging is used to transport substances not subject to these regulations, the words not restricted and the special provision number A152 must be included on the air waybill, if one is issued. For specimens prepared with alcohol or alcohol solutions, the following requirements must be met: 1. Specimens must be: Wrapped in paper towels or cheesecloth moistened with alcohol or an alcohol solution, then placed in a heat-sealed plastic bag. Any free liquid in the bag must not exceed 30 mL; or Placed in vials or other rigid containers with no more than 30 mL of alcohol or an alcohol solution. 2. The prepared specimens must then be placed in a heat-sealed plastic bag. 3. The bagged specimens must be placed inside another plastic bag containing absorbent material, which is then heat-sealed. 4. The final bag must be placed in a strong outer packaging with appropriate cushioning material. 5. The total quantity of flammable liquid per outer packaging must not exceed 1 liter. 6. The completed package must be marked with the words scientific research specimens, not restricted. Special Provision A180 applies. These words, along with the special provision number A180, must also be included on the air waybill, if one is issued. Packing Instructions P620, P650, and P621 are based on the United Nations (UN) model regulations, while Packing Instruction PI954 is derived from the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) technical instructions. These instructions outline specific requirements for the safe transport of infectious substances and other hazardous materials. For Packing Instruction P620: This applies to UN 2814 and UN 2900. Packaging must include: 1. Leakproof primary receptacles. 2. Leakproof secondary packaging. 3. Absorbent material sufficient to absorb the entire contents, placed between the primary receptacle(s) and the secondary packaging. 4. If multiple fragile primary receptacles are used in a single secondary packaging, they must be individually wrapped or separated to prevent contact. 5. A rigid outer packaging, such as drums, boxes, or jerricans, with minimum external dimensions of 100 mm. Additional requirements include: Infectious substances must not be consolidated with unrelated goods in the same inner packaging. If dry ice is used, the outer packaging or overpack must allow the release of carbon dioxide gas to prevent pressure buildup. Primary and secondary packaging must maintain integrity at temperatures ranging from -40°C to +55°C and withstand a pressure differential of at least 95 kPa. For Packing Instruction P650: This applies to UN 3373. Packaging must consist of: 1. A primary receptacle. 2. A secondary packaging. 3. A rigid outer packaging. The packaging must prevent leakage under normal transport conditions and include cushioning material to protect the contents. For liquid substances, absorbent material must be placed between the primary receptacle and the secondary packaging. For solid substances, the primary and secondary packaging must be siftproof. For Packing Instruction P621: This applies to UN 3291. Packaging must include sufficient absorbent material to retain any liquid present and conform to Packing Group II performance standards for solids or liquids. For Packing Instruction PI954: This applies to the transport of dry ice (UN 1845) on passenger and cargo aircraft. Packaging must allow the release of carbon dioxide gas to prevent pressure buildup. The shipper must coordinate with the operator to ensure ventilation safety procedures are followed. Documentation must include the UN number, proper shipping name, number of packages, and net quantity of dry ice in each package. The net mass of dry ice must also be marked on the outside of the package. In all cases, shippers must ensure that packages are prepared to arrive at their destination in good condition and without posing a hazard to persons or animals during transport. An itemized list of contents must be enclosed between the secondary and outer packaging. If infectious substances are suspected to meet the criteria for Category A, the words suspected Category A infectious substance must be included in the shipping documentation. Empty packaging must be disinfected or sterilized before reuse, and any labels indicating previous contents must be removed or obliterated.
